newsitem.title: USA: NIPSCO, IWC Resources to merge.
newsitem.headline: NIPSCO, IWC Resources to merge.

text.p: NIPSCO Industries Inc and IWC Resources Corp said Thursday they signed a definitive agreement under which NIPSCO will acquire IWC's stock for about $288 million, payable primarily in stock.
Each share of IWC stock will be exchanged for $32 of NIPSCO stock. Shareholders will have the option of taking up to 55 percent of the total purchase price in cash.

Completion of the transaction is subject to approval by IWC shareholders. The sale is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 1997. IWC will become a wholly owned subsidiary of NIPSCO.
IWC's largest subsidiary, Indianapolis Water Co, provides water service to about 235,000 customers in Indianapolis and adjacent counties.
In addition, IWC owns the largest underground utility locating and marking service business in the United States and one of the nation's major gas pipeline construction companies.
"Today's announcement is the result of discussions between NIPSCO and IWC Resources that have been ongoing for many months," said IWC chairman James Morris in a statement.

"This merger permits our company to partner with one of the nation's leaders in the gas and electric utility industries and will provide resources for each of our businesses to further grow well into the 21st Century," Morris added.
Hammond, Ind.-based NIPSCO is an energy-based holding company whose regulated subsidiaries provide natural gas and electric services throughout northern Indiana.
NIPSCO ended at 39-3/8, up 3/4, and IWC at 26, up 1-3/4.
